subject: FDA change control plans and model updates
text:

documentation a formal requirement for AI devices with a change control

change.

further this week. Wednesday works best.

subject: who checks the agent's work
text:
Hi [NAME],

We work with a large healthcare payer where reviewers validate AI
recommendations against clinical data, flag errors, and log every
correction.

Every new use case [COMPANY] ships, underwriting, AML, claims, is also a new
place an agent's decision has to hold up in front of a risk committee.
Seems like your team already treats evaluation as a real research problem,
but i know the difficulty is running that same check continuously, across
every customer.

Is that continuous version something you're actively building, or still
closer to ad hoc?

Do you have some time to connect this week to show you how we've helped the
large US payer? If so, let me know and I'll send over a meeting link.

subject: proving it to the next buyer
text:
Hi [NAME],

We work with a large healthcare payer where reviewers validate AI
recommendations against clinical data, flag errors, and log every
correction. Same job [COMPANY] ships in underwriting and AML, just a
different industry. The workload is identical: prove the AI got it right
before a customer sees it.

New capital means lots more use cases before governance catches up. I'm
curious how you're thinking about proving agent accuracy to your next
enterprise buyer, not just your current ones.

Do you have some time to connect this week to show you how we've helped? If
so, let me know and I'll send over a meeting link.

text:

subject: the cost of scaling past oncology
text:
Hi [NAME],

We work with a top 3 US health-services payer on the same core workload as
the Clinical Clarity Engine, checking LLM output against source records
before it becomes a decision.

Following your Series B funding and push for Clinical Clarity Engine into
every clinical domain, your data infrastructure underneath the ML models
becomes critical.

Every new domain is a new place for "decision-ready" to get tested by your
customers. I'm curious how you're thinking about that as the roadmap
expands.

Do you have some time to connect this Thursday to show you what we've done
with the top 3 payer? If so, let me know and I'll send over a meeting link.

subject: two regulatory tracks at once
text:
Hi [NAME],

I saw [COMPANY] close the $70M Series B to fund the US FDA De Novo pathway
alongside the European commercial scale-up. Running both tracks in parallel
means two separate evidence packages, two standards for annotation, and two
audit trails that need to be airtight.

We worked with Conavi Medical, MMI and Moon Surgical on exactly this during
their FDA 510(k) submission.

I'm curious how [COMPANY] is set up to handle that dual-track evidence
burden right now?

Do you have some time to connect this Thursday? If so, let me know and I'll
send over a meeting link.

subject: Safer Road Relies on Better Training Data
text:

At Encord, we work with companies like Flock Safety on annotation and model evaluation for their LPR detection catalogue across hundreds of municipalities. The pattern I've seen working directly with them is that detection accuracy is a training data problem before it's a model problem.

Is that on your radar? If so, let's grab 20 minutes early next week to chat?

subject: hfd consistent across 40 sites
text:
Hi [NAME], 

We just worked with a team who built their own review tooling for star detection and streak tracking, then hit the point where every new ontology change cost them labelled data. 

they moved the review layer to us and kept the models. Given the range you're covering I'd guess a few things get slow: 

• 

Auto-tuning drifts when a telescope's PSF shifts. 

• 

Streak detections near the threshold get judged inconsistently across runs. 

• 

Edge cases end up in a spreadsheet, not a reviewable queue. 

Is any of that familiar or not? Let me know and would be happy to connect and show how we helped!

Please let me know.

subject: multimodal content safety
text:

      [NAME],

subject: LLM post training
text:
Hi 
      [NAME], 

      Came across your work on post-training eval systems for LLMs at [COMPANY] and thought I'd reach out. I work with Thinking Machines Lab and Yutori on similar LLM/agent post-training and SFT workflows. 

      One pattern we're seeing across teams building similar systems is that as RL + synthetic data + LLM/VLM-as-judge pipelines become more critical, the bottleneck becomes maintaining consistency and tructu in the eval signals across the training stack. 

      That's what Frontier Labs works with Encord to build: the infra that makes human rubric based eval, annotator calibration and agreement measurement consistent across modalities and use cases. 

      Would love to get your perspective and share some learnings. Open to a quick 20-min later this week?
